question: Can consolidating ordinary/native execution remove a complete duplicated activation or operand stage?
findings: Both forms already use the same immutable instructions/final positions and shared integer/operator kernels. Compiler forwards adjacent leaves and local-result stores; there is no still-separate operand stack to remove.

Ordinary bound invocation already defers its lexical context. Inline native storage is a stack-backed span for small calls, or already-admitted owned final storage for larger bound calls. The 16-slot buffer is not a general native eligibility cap.

Native prefix cannot survive suspension; it copies live references once only when stack-backed values must escape, preserves its PC and adopts any prepared child. Resumable storage retains owned temporaries and an awaited-disposal queue. These lifetime differences are observable requirements.

There are two opcode routers. Their existence does not establish removable runtime work. Simply merging them would require changing span/resumable storage access or adding a view/dispatch abstraction, with no demonstrated dominant allocation to remove.

Current code still has several context-dependent routing and protocol branches. They need owning whole-script attribution and semantic accounting before any complete-stage migration; no extra entry/default/argument special case is selected here.
decision: Keep the two storage lifetimes and measured native optimizations. Do not blindly merge routers or begin an execution-framework rewrite. Keep the whole-script design objective active; select an actual displaced stage from current owning evidence before prototyping.
measurement: Source gate only: no new elapsed/allocation/CPython measurement or speedup claim. Do not add the failed text experiment to external ratios.
